- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in price decline: if true price drops below 65–68, forecast often stays above 70; apply early correction to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out extreme swings by averaging 3–5 prior days’ sentiment-weighted price trends.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted moving average to anchor forecast near 3–5 day average.
